finite_work.allocation: At most one local setup test, one remote setup test if the actual canonical path performs it, one useful request and one short explicit continuation per topology. Unused slots stay unused; no extra retry turns to chase a desired approval.
finite_work.request: Read only <project>/numbers.csv. Calculate its data row count, sum and SHA-256. Write exactly one JSON object with keys row_count, sum and input_sha256 to <lane_deliverables>/report.json. The deliverables directory is a precreated disposable sibling outside this project writable root but inside the campaign Temp root. Do not change permissions, sandbox, writable roots or global policy to perform this task. If the actual native policy requires a command permission, request it through the native mechanism and wait for the human decision. Do not read or write other paths, use the network, install tools, spawn subagents or retry a denied command with another method.
finite_work.continuation: Using only the existing canonical result, state the reported sum once. Do not run another command or write another file.
finite_work.native_decision: Review one genuine item/commandExecution/requestApproval per topology. Approve only the actual exact command that reads the lane numbers.csv and writes its one report.json. No broad prefix or persistent approval; no policy/sandbox modification. If policy admits the write without a request, record native-decision evidence as pending, not inferred. If denied, do not bypass the decision through another tool or output path.

delivery.non_guarantee: The sibling output can provoke a legitimate native request under a restricting policy, but is not guaranteed to do so. If no qualified request appears, the useful result may pass while the native-decision M1 case remains pending.

accounting_algorithm: Arm and persist the serial campaign reservation before any setup test or productive effect. Include every setup/work/continuation in the global maximum of six.

Replay committed work events through the existing page contract, validating scope, epoch, cursors, watermark and gap. Observe standalone setup journals as a distinct owned source; do not invent canonical binding fields absent there.

A work request may settle observationally only after its correlated turn start, terminal outcome, at least one usage observation and caught-up gap-free replay. This is coverage of the observed prefix, not proof of a final provider/billing counter. Continue monitoring earlier threads for delayed usage.

Missing usage for the completed turn, missing start/terminal, unknown source, cursor gap, regression/reset or malformed data blocks new admissions. Preserve known minimum and request canonical interrupt/close or owned service stop as appropriate to the active scope.

Use the existing preventive100000 observed-token threshold and120-second serial deadline. Additional500000 tolerance over the original200000 does not create a native hard cap or authorize extra turns.
token_accounting.estimated_account_usage_endpoint: Not a substitute for campaign accounting; schema labels its thread usage estimated and the account may include unrelated activity.
token_accounting.limitation: Usage updates are observations after computation. Current TurnStartParams/harness settings expose no hard per-turn/output/aggregate token cap. Interrupt and force contain later, not at an atomically enforced token boundary. A finite number of turns and a large margin do not prove an atomic hard ceiling.

operational_policy.meaning: Stop new admissions and request preventive interruption at 100000 reported aggregate tokens, retaining the conservative threshold. The user allows up to 500000 overshoot over the original 200000 budget, hence 700000 total tolerance. Reporting and interruption remain asynchronous; this is operational monitoring, not an atomic native hard cap. Missing/incomplete accounting stops admission. No extra turns are admitted to consume the allowance. Execution authorization is separate.
